Authorised Materials QC

 

Learn to compare the authorised materials, their conditions, quantities and restrictions, record the result and raise concerns with Senior Delivery.

About 90 minutes 12 sections 14 question self-test

No previous QC experience is needed. It assumes no prior knowledge of eAssessment, eVigilation or the Lookup Tool.

By the end you will be able to:

  • compare the platforms that apply to a unit, field by field
  • set the category and the outcome in the QC sheet
  • write a comment Senior Delivery can act on, and know when to raise something

Your first check is a real row in the sheet, and every unit receives an independent second QC by a Senior Delivery member.

Before your first check, ask your manager for access to the three platforms and the QC sheet.

Your progress is saved in this browser as you go, so you can stop and come back.

Authorised Materials QC · Process

Check that authorised materials agree across the relevant exam platforms and are clear enough for students and supervisors to follow.

Allow about 90 minutes 12 sections 16 worked examples 14 question self-test

Stage 1 of 4 Understand

01

Authorised materials: what they are and why we check them

How to use this guide

Read sections 1 to 12 in order the first time. They follow the order of an authorised materials check, and each step assumes the ones before it have been completed.

  1. Understand 01–02 Learn the purpose, your role and the platforms.
  2. Do 03–07 Prepare, open the platforms, choose the category, compare and record.
  3. Judge 08–11 Learn what happens next, look up terms, and practise with examples.
  4. Keep 12 Use the quick checklist when checking a real exam.

You do not need to memorise the guide. Use the glossary when a term is unfamiliar and keep the field guidance in section 6 beside you during a check. Once you understand the process, use the checklist in section 12 as a reminder of the steps, and search (⌘K) for anything else.

Authorised materials are the resources students are authorised to use during an exam, such as notes, calculators and working sheets. The authorised materials quality check (QC) compares the published list of authorised materials, the instructions and the exam rules before the exam runs, to check that they are consistent across the platforms and can be followed.

Students and supervisors use different platforms to read these instructions.

The authorised materials need to match across the platforms, so that students and supervisors have the same information and the same expectations.

QC identifies discrepancies or problems so they can be reviewed prior to the exam.

Who this guide is forThis guide is for staff carrying out the first QC, the initial check of an exam’s authorised materials.

Your role

Who does what

In this guide, you refers to the staff member carrying out the first QC. An exam supervisor is the person supervising students during the exam. Senior Delivery staff are Matt Nixon and Kayla Sgambellone, who manage second QC and any required follow-up.

Every exam is checked twice. The first QC is yours. The second QC is an independent re-check of every applicable platform by Matt or Kayla, whoever did not do the first check. Section 8 explains it.

Your responsibility is to compare the authorised materials and record your findings in a clear way.

ResponsibilityWho does it
Compare the information across the platforms.You
Record the category, outcome and any supporting comments needed.You
Record any rules or instructions supervisors may need to know about.You
Manage faculty clarification, corrections and supervisor reminders.Senior Delivery

Your job is to record what you find. If the platforms conflict, record it as a discrepancy: you do not have to resolve it yourself. Senior Delivery carries out an independent second QC and handles any clarification or correction.

1

You record, you do not resolve. If instructions conflict or need clarification, record the issue in your comments and tell Senior Delivery by Zoom or a Slack message. Raise it when you find it rather than waiting. They manage the decision or correction. Do not choose which platform should take priority, change exam content or contact the faculty yourself.

2

If the authorised materials or instructions are not clear, write it down. Record differences, unclear instructions and the items listed in section 6 in your comments on the QC sheet, which section 3 introduces. Name the platform and quote the relevant wording. If you need help with the procedure itself, ask Matt or Kayla before guessing an outcome. Section 7 separates the two.

Stage 1 of 4 Understand

02

The platforms you will use

The three platforms you compare, who reads each one, and which apply to each delivery period.

The platforms below show the authorised materials that students and supervisors see. You compare them because each audience needs instructions that mean the same thing. Their layouts differ: an item may appear in a named field on one platform and in free text on another.

Students use this

eAssessment

Check the exam page’s Instructions and Authorised Materials sections. Instructions is free text, so it carries conditions the other platforms have no field for.

Applies to every supervised exam
Online Supervisors use this

eVigilation

Check the Authorised Materials panel, opened from the information icon. Its fields are fixed, so wording that does not fit a field appears in free text, usually under Other.

Applies to every supervised exam
In-Venue Supervisors use this

Lookup Tool

Check the unit card in Authorised Materials Search, read on tablets at the venue. Use it for the end of semester QC only.

Applies to end of semester exams only, not Malaysian sittings

Which platforms apply

The delivery period determines whether you compare two platforms or three. Establish it before opening the platforms, then make sure each one shows the same exam shell. An apparent materials mismatch may simply belong to a different sitting.

Use the delivery period in Course Name col A. For example, Sem 1 Deferred & Supplementary is a Deferred and Supplementary exam, not a Semester 1 main exam.

Scroll the table sideways to compare the columns.

Delivery periodPlatforms to compareNotes
Semester 1 or Semester 2
main exam period		Three. eAssessment, eVigilation and the Lookup Tool.These are the exams In-Venue Supervisors invigilate, which is why the Lookup Tool applies. Malaysian sittings are the exception: see below.
Other deliveries
in-semester, Deferred and Supplementary, Rescheduled Deferred, Monash College, external clients		Two. eAssessment and eVigilation.A card in the Lookup Tool may exist for another delivery period, but it does not need to be checked.
Malaysian sittingsTwo. eAssessment and eVigilation, in every delivery period, including Semester 1 and Semester 2.Malaysian units can have their own shell, and their materials can differ from the Australian sitting. Check each shell independently and make sure you open the right eAssessment shell.

Stage 2 of 4 Do

03

Before you start a check

Find a row that is ready to check and that nobody has done yet, and learn the columns you fill in.

Where the work is recorded

Record your findings in the Authorised Materials QC 2026 sheet. The sheet lists the exams to check and holds the results of the checks. Its columns are set out below.

Not a platformThe QC sheet is where you record your findings. It is not one of the platforms you compare.

The QC sheet is your starting point. Each row represents one exam shell, a particular instance of an exam in eAssessment. A unit can have several shells for different groups or sittings.

Getting access

Before your first session, check your access to eAssessment, eVigilation, the Lookup Tool and the QC sheet. If you do not have access, please see Matt or Kayla.

Find the rows to check

Rows are not allocated to you. Enrolment Status col F decides what to action: a row is ready for first QC once it reads Enrolled and Synced. Ready is not the same as unchecked, so read col G, col H and col I before you start. Working by exam date also helps you find the corresponding entry in each platform, since eVigilation and the Lookup Tool both need a date set before they return anything.

  1. Open the Authorised Materials QC 2026 sheet. The Enrolled and Synced Shells tab lists the shells that are ready for a first QC.

  2. Filter Start Time col E to one exam date, then sort Course Name col A alphabetically.

  3. Confirm Enrolment Status col F reads Enrolled and Synced. That is the only test for readiness.

  4. If col G, col H or col I already contains information, ask Senior Delivery before changing it.

For an unchecked row marked Not Enrolled, skip the check and leave G, H and I blank. If the exam is within a week, raise it with Matt or Kayla. Do not clear existing entries.

When QC happens

StageWhat it means for you
Shell built, Not EnrolledNot ready. Leave G, H and I blank. Do not record a discrepancy and do not open the platforms.
Enrolled and SyncedReady to QC. This is the trigger. Work through units in Start Time order.
First QC recordedCategory, outcome and comments are in. The unit is now visible to Senior Delivery through the QC Overview tab.
Second QC recordedcol J is set. Either the unit is complete, or it is with the faculty.

What one check covers

Check Australian, Malaysian, AAA and other shells separately, even when they share a unit code. The shell name in col A tells you which one you have.

For that shell you produce three things, and nothing else: a category in col G, an outcome in col H, and the Comments in col I.

The columns you use

Every result is recorded in the Authorised Materials QC 2026 sheet. Columns A to F are populated automatically. You complete G, H and I; section 7 explains the entries.

ColNameUseWho fills it
ACourse NameIdentify the unit, period, sitting and cohort.Automatic
BLinkOpen the eAssessment shell.Automatic
CStatusWhere the shell sits in the build process. You do not need it to decide whether a row is ready.Automatic
DInvig TypeRead the supervision type.Automatic
EStart TimeSelect the exam date and check how soon it runs.Automatic
FEnrolment StatusThis is what decides readiness. Enrolled and Synced means the row is ready to check.Automatic
GAuth Mat CategorySelect the category that matches the authorised materials.You
HFirst QC OutcomeSelect the result of your comparison.You
ICommentsRecord findings, relevant authorised materials and supporting wording.You
J onwardsSenior Delivery columnsLeave the orange columns to Matt or Kayla.Senior Delivery

Write so the unit can be identifiedSenior Delivery works from what you write, so describe authorised materials in the words the exam page uses, and write generative AI as Gen AI. A unit described vaguely is harder to find when reminders and escalations are decided.

How to complete a check

Work through one exam at a time.

  1. Find its row in the QC sheet and check that the exam is ready to review.

  2. Open the platforms required for its delivery period: eAssessment and eVigilation, plus the Lookup Tool for end of semester exams, except Malaysian sittings.

  3. Compare the authorised materials, rules and instructions. Check that the platforms match and that the instructions are clear enough to follow.

  4. Record the category, comparison outcome and supporting comments. Raise concerns with Senior Delivery for follow-up if required.

Stage 2 of 4 Do

04

Opening the applicable platforms

Choose the delivery period, then open each platform that applies in turn.

Section 2 sets out which platforms apply to each delivery period.

Choose the path for this delivery period

Select the delivery path before following the steps below, and the guide will show only the steps that apply to it.

  1. Open eAssessment from the link in col B. Confirm the shell name on the page matches col A, including the sitting and cohort. These deliveries have more shells per unit than end of semester does, so this check matters more here. A single unit can have an Australian and a Malaysian sitting, a main cohort and an AAA cohort, and a deferred shell, all in the same window.

Open eAssessment

  1. Open Link col B in the QC sheet.

  2. Check that the shell matches Course Name col A, including the period, sitting and cohort.

  3. Read the category and every item under Authorised Materials.

  4. Read Instructions, including conditions on devices, software and copying.

  5. Compare the two sections. If they conflict, record both statements, continue the comparison and include all findings. Raise the conflict with Senior Delivery.

Open eVigilation

  1. Open Exam sessions.

  2. Set Select a date to the exam date in Start Time col E.

  3. Set Search by to Exam unit. Use Session to browse a whole date.

  4. Enter the unit code and search.

  5. Select the information icon on the correct row.

  6. Read the category and all fields: Calculator, Dictionary, Notes, Other, Permitted Item, Textbook and Working Sheets. Read the wording beneath each indicator.

  7. Scroll to the bottom and check Hybrid.

Open the Lookup Tool for end of semester only

The Lookup Tool is the third platform for end of semester exams, and In-Venue Supervisors refer to it on their tablets. It is shown here because you have the end of semester period selected.

  1. Open the Authorised Materials Search at authmats.evigilation.monash.edu.

  2. Set Exam Date to the date in the QC sheet.

  3. Search the unit code and open its card.

  4. Confirm the shell matches Course Name col A, including the delivery period.

  5. Read every field and compare it with eAssessment and eVigilation.

If a unit is missingCheck the exam date and Enrolment Status col F first. A missing eVigilation entry alone does not confirm that an exam is unsupervised. If the row is Enrolled and Synced but the platform remains unavailable, explain what happened in Comments col I and tell Senior Delivery by Zoom or a Slack message. Follow Example 12 in section 11.

Stage 2 of 4 Do

05

Authorised materials categories

The six categories an exam can be, and how to choose the one you record.

The category describes the overall access to materials, such as Closed Book or Open Book. Individual conditions give the detail, including note limits and named software. Read both: a category heading alone does not tell you everything that is authorised or restricted. Choose the category from the materials the exam permits and record any conflict with the published heading as a Discrepancy. Open Access and Open Access with Additional Device are distinct categories, not interchangeable labels.

CategoryWhat it permitsCheck
Closed BookNo resources are permitted.Instructions do not permit items that conflict with the category.
Closed Book + SPIA specified set of items, such as a calculator or limited notes.Each item and its conditions.
Open BookHardcopy reference materials, such as books, notes and dictionaries.Any permission for digital material.
Open Book with Additional DeviceOpen Book materials plus a laptop, tablet or monitor, not a phone.Device type, permitted use and internet conditions. Do not assume connectivity.
Open AccessBroad access to resources, subject to the exam’s restrictions.Gen AI and any other exclusions.
Open Access with Additional DeviceOpen Access plus a laptop, tablet or monitor, not a phone.Device type, permitted use and restrictions.

Category

Compare the category headings and the items each platform permits. Set col G from the authorised materials.

Record it this wayIf a category heading conflicts with the authorised materials listed, record a Discrepancy in col H and quote both in Comments col I.

Where the platforms conflict on the authorised materials themselves, still enter the exam’s most likely category in col G and describe the conflict in Comments. Do not leave col G blank while Senior Delivery resolves it. Ask Senior Delivery if the category is unclear.

Previous4. Opening the applicable platformsNext6. Comparing what the platforms say

Stage 2 of 4 Do

06

Comparing what the platforms say

A field by field comparison of every platform that applies.

In this section
  • Compare fields
  • Always record
  • Where items sit
Delivery period End of semester. Compare eAssessment, eVigilation and the Lookup Tool. All other deliveries. Compare eAssessment and eVigilation. The Lookup Tool does not apply. Change

How to compare

Compare eAssessment and eVigilation. For end of semester exams, also compare the Lookup Tool. Check one field at a time across every applicable platform so you can compare the whole entry before moving to the next item.

Ask two questions. Do the platforms allow the same materials under the same conditions? Could a student and supervisor understand and apply those conditions? Matching words do not settle the second question. If a permitted item or condition remains unclear, record the wording for Senior Delivery to review.

Compare these fields

Jump to a field
  • eA against itself
  • Calculator
  • Dictionary
  • Notes
  • Textbook
  • Working sheets
  • Other / Permitted
  • Additional device
  • Generative AI
  • Answer sheets, Hybrid
  • Copying, translation
  • Sitting and cohort

Decide if the wording conflicts

FindingWhat to do
Categories, authorised materials, restrictions or quantities conflict, within a platform or between platforms.Record a Discrepancy, quote the conflict and continue checking the remaining fields. For example, eA permits 5 working sheets and the Lookup Tool says 99, meaning unlimited (Example 3).
Different words describe the same item.Do not treat wording differences as a discrepancy. Record the comparison where relevant. For example, eVig says Notes - Double sided A4 x 1 - Physical Only and eA says one double sided A4 page of physical notes (Example 5).
The same item is recorded in a different field, such as under Other rather than its named field. Other is where eVigilation and the Lookup Tool put anything that does not fit a named field.Not a discrepancy. Record Other and say in Comments which field the item is sitting in. For example, eVig Notes reads None but Other permits the same notes (Example 4).
Only one platform has a place to state something, and the others say nothing about it.Silence alone is not a discrepancy. Check Other and Permitted Item for anything opposing, then record what the platform that states it says. For example, a copy and paste restriction appears only in eAssessment Instructions (Example 9).
The platforms agree, but the instruction is unclear, contradictory or unusual enough to need review.Record All Match but Escalation Required, explain the concern and raise it with Senior Delivery. For example, a mobile phone permission (Example 16), or pens and pencils with no paper described (Example 15).

For each field below, also check the Lookup Tool card when it applies.

eAssessment against itself

Compare Instructions with Authorised Materials. Record any conflict, quoting both statements.

Keep goingContinue comparing the remaining fields and record all findings. Raise the conflict with Senior Delivery; do not decide which statement takes priority.

Calculator

Check the Calculator field, Instructions and Other. Compare physical or virtual calculators, named products and model restrictions. Record the type when the platforms differ or the wording is unclear, such as “faculty approved calculator”.

A physical calculator and Excel listed under Other are two separate authorised items. Do not assume other calculator software is allowed.

Dictionary

Check whether a dictionary is permitted and whether any type is specified. Read Other as well as Dictionary. Record anything that conflicts; do not assume why a field is empty or says None.

Notes

Compare the permitted format and any stated limits: size, quantity, single or double sided, physical or digital, and handwritten or printed. Record the wording where it differs between platforms, or a limit is unclear.

Different wording can describe the same item. If all platforms permit “one folder of printed notes” without a page count, record the wording in Comments; this alone does not require escalation.

Record it this wayIf a Notes field says None but Other permits the same notes the other platforms state, that is the same item in a different field, not a disagreement. Record Other and say in Comments which field it is sitting in.

Textbook

Compare the Textbook field and any named book or edition in Instructions or Other. Record anything that conflicts or any different restriction.

Working sheets

Read the Working Sheets field and any quantity in Instructions. Record each platform’s wording or number where they differ.

ValueMeaning
YesWorking sheets are permitted. This value alone gives no quantity.
A specified count, such as 5That number of working sheets.
99 in the Lookup ToolUnlimited working sheets.
UnlimitedNo quantity limit.
No, None, 0, N/A or NANo working sheets.

5 against Yes is not a discrepancy on that difference alone, because Yes can accompany a limited or unlimited number. 5 against 99 is a discrepancy, because five differs from unlimited. Compare any additional restrictions in the platforms.

Keep it to this fieldDo not apply these working-sheet conversions to answer sheets or any other field.

Other and Permitted Item

Other is where eVigilation and the Lookup Tool put anything that does not fit a named field. Read both fields and eAssessment Instructions in full. Look for software, formula sheets, unusual items and restrictions. Compare their meaning with the rest of the page and the other platforms. Record relevant wording.

Record it this wayA formula sheet mentioned or provided but absent from the authorised materials list is a Discrepancy. This applies whether it is embedded in the exam, separately linked or a hard copy the student brings to the exam sitting. Record its type, page count and how it is accessed.

Additional device

Check the device permission in Instructions: device type, allowed use, internet access and limits on communication, Gen AI or applications. Check other platforms’ free-text fields for opposing conditions. Record the exact wording and raise missing or conflicting conditions.

Escalate this onePermission to use a mobile phone during the assessment requires escalation to Senior Delivery, even if the platforms agree. Routine instructions to photograph or upload hybrid answers after the exam do not require escalation on that basis alone.

Generative AI

Check whether Gen AI is permitted or prohibited, including any limits on its use. Compare every applicable platform and record the wording. Use Gen AI permitted or Gen AI prohibited so the comment is clear.

Permission to use a named application does not necessarily permit all its AI functions. Record unclear limits rather than deciding them yourself.

Silence is a findingIf no applicable platform mentions Gen AI, record Gen AI not stated and raise it. Faculties are required to specify, so silence is not an approved default. Where the platforms otherwise agree, this is the All Match but Escalation Required case.

Answer sheets and Hybrid

Check Hybrid at the bottom of eVigilation and read the answer sheet instructions in eAssessment. Compare any stated answer sheet quantities. Record conflicting counts, or a paper component with no clear answer sheet instructions.

Record the Hybrid flag and each platform’s count separately. Hybrid yes or no is not a quantity. Note: answer sheets are not working sheets.

Escalate this oneIf all platforms permit pens and pencils but describe no working or answer sheets, and Hybrid is No, record the contradiction in Comments and escalate to Senior Delivery. Use All Match but Escalation Required for that case.

Copying and translation restrictions

Copy and paste restrictions appear in eAssessment Instructions. eVigilation and the Lookup Tool carry the basic instructions and authorised materials and have no field for them, so record the restriction as eAssessment states it. Their silence is not disagreement.

Use COPY AND PASTE RESTRICTIONS as a comment label, followed by the actual rule. Translation is different: another platform can state a translation permission in a free-text field, so compare it and record any opposing statement. A ban on browser extensions can coexist with permission for a separate translation website.

Sitting and cohort

Check that what you are reading on every platform belongs to the shell in Course Name col A. If it is for another sitting or cohort, open the correct one before comparing the authorised materials.

Always record these items

These are the conditions only one platform can note, so an All Match outcome does not capture them. Record them in Comments col I even when the platforms agree. Calculator, notes and working sheets appear on every platform, so you compare them rather than record them. Record those only when something about them needs flagging.

ItemInclude
Gen AIPermission or prohibition and any conditions. If no platform mentions it, record that it is not stated.
Copy and pasteThe exact restriction.
TranslationTools, websites and device conditions.
SoftwareNames, packages and where they may run.
Formula sheetsType, page count and how students receive or access them.
Local files and MoodleNamed files or the scope of permitted access.
Additional deviceDevice type, permitted use and restrictions.
Unfamiliar itemsWhat is permitted and where it is noted.

Check where each item is recorded

An item may appear in Other rather than its named field. This generally happens because eVigilation fields have length limits. Read both before deciding whether the platforms agree. A discrepancy is when the platforms say different things. The same item recorded in a different field is not one: record Other and say in Comments which field it is in.

Stage 2 of 4 Do

07

Recording the result

Three cells belong to you: what each one is for, how they differ, and the conditions supervisors need to know about.

Delivery period End of semester. Compare eAssessment, eVigilation and the Lookup Tool. All other deliveries. Compare eAssessment and eVigilation. The Lookup Tool does not apply. Change

Three different things

The three entries answer different questions. Category describes the exam’s authorised materials, outcome describes your comparison, and comments explain the finding. The same category can have a matching result or a discrepancy; choosing a category does not establish that the platforms agree.

ColumnWhat it records
Auth Mat Category col GWhat the exam permits.
First QC Outcome col HWhat the comparison found.
Comments col IThe supporting wording, findings and items listed in section 6.

A matching exam can still need comments and a supervisor reminder. Senior Delivery decides on reminders separately from the QC outcome.

  1. Set Auth Mat Category col G to the category the exam actually is.

  2. Set First QC Outcome col H. All Match (eVig, eA, Lookup) is still the correct value when both platforms agree and what they agree on can be acted on, despite the name.

  3. Write what you found in Comments col I: anything other than a clean match, plus the items in the Always record list, even when every platform agrees. Name each platform and quote its wording.

Choose the first QC outcome

Choose the outcome from the check as a whole. One conflicting category, item or quantity is enough for Discrepancy even if the remaining fields agree. When platforms agree but an unclear, contradictory or unusual instruction needs review, use All Match but Escalation Required and explain why. If you could not complete the comparison, follow When you need help below.

OutcomeUse it when
All Match (eVig, eA, Lookup)All applicable platforms agree, the instructions can be followed and no concern requires escalation. Record the always-record items in section 6. See Examples 2, 5 and 9.
DiscrepancyCategories, authorised materials, restrictions or quantities conflict within or between platforms, or a formula sheet is missing from the authorised materials list. Quote the finding. See Examples 1, 3 and 10.
All Match but Escalation RequiredPlatforms agree, but an unclear, contradictory or unusual instruction needs review. Explain the concern and raise it with Senior Delivery. See Examples 15 and 16.
OtherA completed check does not fit another outcome: the authorised materials are complex or vague, or you need clarification on something. Explain why in Comments. See Example 4.
Unsupervised ExamThe assessment has no supervision. Ask Matt or Kayla to confirm this before you use it, and record the confirmation in Comments.

The value name lists three platformsUse All Match (eVig, eA, Lookup) for a matching two-platform check too. The dropdown label does not change which platforms apply.

When you need help

SituationWhat to do
Unclear published wordingQuote it in Comments. Use Discrepancy if the platforms conflict, or All Match but Escalation Required if they agree but need clarification.
A required platform will not open, or an Enrolled and Synced unit remains missingExplain what happened in Comments col I, then tell Senior Delivery by Zoom or a Slack message. Do not guess a category or outcome from an incomplete comparison.
A procedure or field is unfamiliarAsk Matt or Kayla before recording the result.
An exam that looks unsupervisedDo not record it as unsupervised yet. Ask Matt or Kayla to confirm its status first. A missing eVigilation entry is not enough.
A row marked Not EnrolledIt is not ready to check. Skip it and leave G, H and I blank, as in section 3.

Write a useful comment

Write enough for another checker to find the issue without asking what you meant. Name each platform, quote only the relevant wording and say what needs attention. A comment such as “notes do not match” is too vague.

Too vagueWrite this instead
Notes do not matchNotes: eA permits “one double sided A4 page of physical notes”. eVig permits the same page, recorded under Other, with the Notes field reading “None”. Same notes, different field.
Calculator does not matchCalculator: eA and eVig specify a physical calculator. Lookup says “faculty approved calculator”; the permitted type needs clarification.
Platforms disagree on translationTranslation: eA permits an online translation website for single words. eVig Other says “No translation tools permitted”.

Your record supports the next stage of the work. Escalation means referring an issue for a decision or clarification. A supervisor reminder draws attention to a condition that needs to be noticed during the exam. Clear, matching authorised materials can need a reminder without needing faculty clarification. Senior Delivery manages both types of follow-up.

Supervisor reminders

You do not decide on, write or send supervisor reminders: Senior Delivery does. Your part is to record the conditions a reminder might be based on, as in the table below.

ConditionWhat you record in Comments
The category is Open Access with Additional DeviceThe device wording from the exam page: what the device may be, and what it may hold or reach.
The unit permits generative AIThe string Gen AI, spelled as two words. Record it whether or not the platforms agree with each other.
The exam page carries copy and paste restrictionsThe restriction in the wording the page uses. Record it in capitals as COPY AND PASTE RESTRICTIONS, which is the form used in the QC sheet.

These are the situations currently visible in the QC sheet, and they are not a closed list. Senior Delivery decides which units receive a reminder, so record any condition a supervisor would need to know about in advance, whether or not it appears above.

Senior Delivery works from the QC Overview tab, which is built from your Comments. Describe each condition clearly so the reminder reaches the right unit.

Second QC Outcome col J

Senior Delivery completes Second QC Outcome col J and the orange columns. Section 8 explains the second check.

Stage 3 of 4 Judge

08

Second QC

What happens after your first QC, and what to raise before the exam.

The second QC

Every unit receives a second QC by a Senior Delivery member who did not perform the first check. They independently check every applicable platform and record the result in col J. Your comments support that check; they do not replace it.

RuleDetail
Every unit is checked twiceThe second QC is a full re-check of the authorised materials, instructions and exam rules, not a review of your comment. It applies to every row, including those you recorded as a clean match.
The second pass is independentIt is completed by a different person, so a unit is never signed off by the person who first checked it.
The result is recorded in col JSenior Delivery records the second QC outcome. You do not complete this column.

Write your comments for a reader who has not seen the exam page. Naming each platform and quoting its wording is what lets the reviewer compare their own reading against yours.

Follow up before the exam

Raise anything you find as soon as you find it, in the Comments column and then by Zoom or a Slack message to Matt or Kayla. The week before the exam is a backstop, not a waiting period. Raise these with Matt or Kayla when the exam is within a week:

1

The unit still has no first QC outcome.

2

A discrepancy or escalation remains unresolved. A faculty needs time to answer.

3

The unit is still marked Not Enrolled.

Start early enough to allow the second QC and any faculty response. A first QC completed the day before an exam leaves no time for either.

Check for new rows

After finishing an exam date, check for units added since you filtered. Use the Enrolled and Synced Shells and QC Overview tabs to find outstanding work, then continue to the next exam date.

Stage 3 of 4 Judge

09

Glossary

The terms used throughout this process, to look up whenever one is unfamiliar.

The terms you will meet most oftenExam shell, Enrolled and Synced, discrepancy and Senior Delivery. Use the table below as a reference when these or any other term is unfamiliar.

The glossary is alphabetical. Terms are also explained where they first matter, so you do not need to memorise this page.

TermDefinition
AAAAlternative Assessment Arrangements, such as extra time or specialised equipment. Students with AAA can be in a separate exam shell, which is checked on its own row.
Authorised materialsThe list of materials students are authorised to use during their eExam, and the terms on which they may use them: how many of each item, and the conditions and restrictions attached. All of this information is compared, not the items alone. See section 6.
CohortA group of students sitting in the same session or the same unit code.
Centrally scheduled examsExams timetabled by Assessment Scheduling. This does not, by itself, determine whether the Lookup Tool applies; use section 2.
DiscrepancyA conflict in categories, authorised materials, restrictions or quantities, within a platform or between platforms. The same item recorded in a different field is not a discrepancy. A formula sheet that is provided but missing from the authorised materials list is also a discrepancy.
eAThe eAssessment platform. This abbreviation appears in comments and outcome labels.
Enrolled and SyncedThe status showing that the shell is ready to check. See section 3.
eVigThe eVigilation platform. This abbreviation appears in comments and outcome labels.
eVigNS / eVigRSeVigilation notation for no scan and room scan supervision.
Exam shellOne instance of an exam in eAssessment. Each shell needs its own check.
Gen AIGenerative artificial intelligence. Record whether the exam permits Gen AI or not.
HybridAn exam with a paper answer component: at least one question in the eExam requires a handwritten response. Check the answer sheet instructions separately from working sheets.
In-semester assessmentAn assessment during teaching, outside the main exam periods. Compare eAssessment and eVigilation.
Invig TypeThe supervision type in col D. Ask Senior Delivery if a code is unfamiliar.
Lookup ToolThe Authorised Materials Search tool that In-Venue Supervisors may use. A QC platform for end of semester exams only, except Malaysian sittings. See section 2.
Not EnrolledThe exam shell is not ready to check. See section 3.
Senior DeliveryMatt Nixon and Kayla Sgambellone. They manage the orange columns, second QC and escalation.
SPISpecifically Permitted Items: specific resources students can refer to in a closed book eExam, as in Closed Book + SPI.
SittingOne delivery of an exam for a particular location or time.
Unsupervised examAn assessment with no supervision. Before recording an exam as unsupervised, ask Matt or Kayla to confirm its status; see section 7.
Working sheetsBlank sheets for working out during an exam. These are separate from hybrid answer sheets.

Stage 3 of 4 Judge

10

One check, worked through

A single check from the row in the sheet to the three cells filled in. Read it before the self-test.

This example connects the steps you have just learned, from choosing the correct platforms to writing the three entries. Notice how each entry follows from the comparison, and why Comments may still contain detail when the outcome is All Match.

A teaching example, not a real rowIt is illustrative, not a real unit or a scored question. The rules applied to it are the ones set out in sections 3 to 8. Work through it by reading, then use section 11 to test the decisions.

  1. Check the row. The shell is ACC2100 2026 Sem 1 Deferred & Supplementary. col F reads Enrolled and Synced; col G, col H and col I are empty.

  2. Choose the platforms. Deferred and Supplementary uses eAssessment and eVigilation.

  3. Read eAssessment. The category is Closed Book + SPI. Both Authorised Materials and Instructions permit a physical calculator and one double sided A4 page of physical notes. Working sheets: None. Instructions also prohibit copying between the notes and response box. No paper answer component is described.

  4. Read eVigilation. The category and physical calculator match. Notes reads Notes - Double sided A4 x 1 - Physical Only. Working Sheets reads None. Dictionary, Textbook, Other and Permitted Item contain nothing further. Hybrid reads no.

  5. Compare. The notes wording means the same thing. The working sheet quantities match. All other applicable fields agree, and the stated authorised materials are clear. The copying restriction sits in eAssessment Instructions, where it belongs.

  6. Record the result as shown below.

What goes in the three cells

Nothing here disagrees, so the only thing worth recording is the copying restriction. It is stated in eAssessment, which is the only platform with a place for it.

col GClosed Book + SPI col HAll Match (eVig, eA, Lookup) col ICOPY AND PASTE RESTRICTIONS: eA Instructions prohibit copying between the notes and response box.

What happens nextSenior Delivery carries out the second QC and decides whether the copying restriction needs a reminder. Neither is yours to complete.

Worked examples and self-test

Sixteen cases for reference, fourteen of them scored. Test yourself hides each classification until you commit to an answer.

0 of 14 answered

There are 16 cases and 14 scored questions. Examples 6 and 8 are reference cases. The pass mark is 12 out of 14, using first-attempt answers.

For each case, identify the permission or restriction, compare the platforms and decide what needs recording. Use the earlier sections when needed; the questions practise applying the process.

Use Test yourself to answer before revealing the explanation. Reference shows the worked answers. Where a case says All Match, assume the other applicable fields agree, can be followed and raise no separate concern requiring escalation.

DiscrepancyAn additional device▸
What you see
The eAssessment heading reads Open Access. Instructions permit a laptop or tablet, not a phone, with internet access. eVigilation has no device instruction; the other details agree.
What to do
Select Open Access with Additional Device in col G. Open Access is a different category, so record the heading conflict as Discrepancy in col H. Include the device permission and conflicting heading in Comments.
What to enter
col GOpen Access with Additional Devicecol HDiscrepancycol IeA permits an internet-connected laptop or tablet, not a phone. This fits Open Access with Additional Device, but the eA heading reads Open Access. eVig has no device instruction.

Based on the stated permissions, which value belongs in Auth Mat Category, col G?

All MatchGenerative AI permission▸
What you see
eAssessment, eVigilation and the Lookup card explicitly permit Gen AI. The permission is clear and consistent, with no conflicting instruction.
What to do
Select All Match and record the permission. Senior Delivery decides whether a reminder is needed. A clear permission does not need faculty clarification merely because it concerns Gen AI.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match (eVig, eA, Lookup)col IGen AI permitted in eA Instructions, eVig and Lookup. All three agree.

All platforms agree. What belongs in First QC Outcome, col H?

DiscrepancyWorking sheet quantities▸
What you see
eAssessment permits 5 working sheets. eVigilation says Yes. The Lookup card says 99.
What to do
Yes confirms permission without a quantity. 99 means unlimited. The discrepancy is between eAssessment’s five-sheet limit and the Lookup Tool’s unlimited permission.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HDiscrepancycol IWorking sheets: eA permits 5; eVig says Yes, with no quantity; Lookup says 99, meaning unlimited. eA and Lookup quantities conflict.

What belongs in First QC Outcome, col H?

OtherNotes recorded in the wrong field▸
What you see
eAssessment permits “one double sided A4 page of physical notes”. eVigilation Notes reads None, and Other permits the same page of notes.
What to do
The platforms permit the same thing, so this is not a discrepancy. eVigilation fields have length limits, so a faculty sometimes has to put a permission in Other because it will not fit where it belongs. Record Other and say in Comments which field the permission is sitting in.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HOthercol INotes: eA and eVig both permit “one double sided A4 page of physical notes”. In eVig it is recorded under Other and the Notes field reads “None”. Same permission, different field.

Both platforms permit the same page of notes, but eVig records it under Other. What belongs in First QC Outcome, col H?

All MatchDifferent words with the same meaning▸
What you see
eVigilation says Notes - Double sided A4 x 1 - Physical Only. eAssessment says “One double sided A4 page of physical notes is permitted.”
What to do
Both describe the same size, quantity and format. Select All Match. Nothing here needs recording: the wording differs but the permission is identical and both platforms state it.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match (eVig, eA, Lookup)col INo entry needed. The notes wording differs between eVig and eA but states the same permission.

What belongs in First QC Outcome, col H?

Escalation RequiredUndefined notes permission▸
What you see
The applicable platforms agree that “open notes” are permitted. Neither the exam page nor the unit’s other published information defines the phrase.
What to do
Record the wording and request clarification through Senior Delivery. Do not borrow a definition from another unit. If this unit publishes a clear definition that resolves the uncertainty, record it and reassess the outcome.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match but Escalation Requiredcol IAll platforms permit “open notes”, but no definition was found in the unit’s published information. The permitted format and limits need clarification.
All MatchA physical calculator and Excel▸
What you see
eAssessment and eVigilation both list a physical calculator under Calculator and Excel under Other.
What to do
The permissions match. Record both the calculator and Excel. Their placement in different fields does not create a discrepancy or permit other unnamed software.
What to enter
col GClosed Book + SPIcol HAll Match (eVig, eA, Lookup)col IPhysical calculator permitted in both platforms. Excel appears under Other in both.

What belongs in First QC Outcome, col H?

DiscrepancyA formula sheet▸
What you see
The exam mentions or provides a formula sheet that is absent from the authorised materials list.
What to do
Record Discrepancy whether the sheet is embedded in the exam, separately linked or brought by the student. Record its type, page count, how students access it and the missing list entry.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HDiscrepancycol IFormula sheet: [type and pages], accessed [where or how]. Not listed under authorised materials. Exam wording: “[quote]”.
All MatchCopy and paste restrictions▸
What you see
eAssessment Instructions prohibit copying between the notes and response box. eVigilation and the Lookup Tool have no field for copy and paste restrictions.
What to do
Silence alone is not a discrepancy. Record the restriction. Senior Delivery decides whether a supervisor reminder is needed.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match (eVig, eA, Lookup)col ICOPY AND PASTE RESTRICTIONS: eA Instructions prohibit copying between the notes and response box.

No other platform has a field for this restriction. Is their silence a Discrepancy?

DiscrepancyOpposing translation permissions▸
What you see
eAssessment permits an online translation website for single words. eVigilation Other says “No translation tools permitted”.
What to do
These are opposing permissions. Record Discrepancy and quote both. This differs from banning browser translation extensions while allowing a separate website, which can be consistent.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HDiscrepancycol IeA permits an online translation website for single words. eVig Other: “No translation tools permitted”.

What belongs in First QC Outcome, col H?

All MatchSeparate shells for one unit▸
What you see
You are checking the main cohort shell in col A. Its platforms agree. The unit also has an AAA shell on a separate row and date.
What to do
Check this row independently. Another shell for the same unit does not create a discrepancy or share this outcome.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match (eVig, eA, Lookup)col IMain cohort shell matches col A. The AAA shell is a separate row and check. [Add the relevant always-record items.]

Does the AAA shell existing make this row a Discrepancy?

Investigate firstA unit missing from eVigilation▸
What you see
A unit in the QC sheet cannot be found in eVigilation. You have not checked the possible causes.
What to do
First confirm the exam date filter. Next check Enrolment Status col F. For an unchecked Not Enrolled row, skip and leave G, H and I blank; raise it with Matt or Kayla if the exam is within a week. If the assessment might be unsupervised, ask Matt or Kayla to confirm its status. If an Enrolled and Synced unit remains missing, explain the issue in Comments and tell Senior Delivery by Zoom or a Slack message.
Recording
If Matt or Kayla confirm it is unsupervised, set col H to Unsupervised Exam and record that confirmation in col I. For an Enrolled and Synced unit whose absence remains unexplained, write in col I which platform and unit could not be found, note that the date was checked, and inform Senior Delivery. Do not guess an outcome or treat the unit as unsupervised.

What do you do first?

All MatchSoftware running locally▸
What you see
All applicable platforms permit the same named software, such as Mathematica, R or Visual Studio, running from the student’s local drive.
What to do
Record the software and where it runs: on the student’s machine rather than a browser or cloud service. This is an always-record item in section 6. Senior Delivery decides on reminders under section 7.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match (eVig, eA, Lookup)col ISoftware: [names], permitted to run locally on the student’s machine. All applicable platforms agree.

The platforms agree. What is your responsibility for this unit?

All MatchA folder of notes▸
What you see
All applicable platforms permit “one folder of printed notes” with no page count. There is no conflicting instruction.
What to do
Select All Match and record the wording in Comments. The absence of a page count does not by itself require escalation.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match (eVig, eA, Lookup)col INotes: “one folder of printed notes”, with no page count. Same permission in all applicable platforms.

The platforms agree. What belongs in First QC Outcome, col H?

Escalation RequiredWriting equipment without paper instructions▸
What you see
All three platforms permit pens and pencils. None describes working sheets or answer sheets, and Hybrid reads No.
What to do
Record the contradiction in Comments and escalate to Senior Delivery. Select All Match but Escalation Required: the platforms agree, but the writing permission lacks paper instructions.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match but Escalation Requiredcol IPens and pencils permitted. No working or answer sheets described in any applicable platform; Hybrid No. Please clarify what students may write on.

All applicable platforms agree and paper provision has been checked. What belongs in col H?

Escalation RequiredA mobile phone permission▸
What you see
All applicable platforms permit using a mobile phone during the assessment, beyond photographing or uploading hybrid answers afterwards.
What to do
Record the unusual permission and escalate to Senior Delivery. Select All Match but Escalation Required, even though the platforms agree. Routine hybrid instructions to photograph or upload answers after the exam do not require escalation on that basis alone.
What to enter
col GThe category supported by the authorised materialscol HAll Match but Escalation Requiredcol IAll applicable platforms permit mobile phone use during the assessment, beyond the normal hybrid answer-upload process. Unusual permission raised with Senior Delivery for review.

The platforms agree on this phone permission. What belongs in First QC Outcome, col H?
